clue.text: Undercover family needs it to change

parts.note: a clan is an extended family group

indicators.note: the letters of 'needs it' are told to change, so they are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written, as anagram fodder

explanation.surface: A spy household must alter its identity to stay undercover.
explanation.walkthrough: 'needs' looks like the verb joining the parts, but both it and 'it' are the letters to be shuffled.
explanation.definitionFit: Something clandestine is secret and covert, as undercover work is.

clue.text: Person at last getting a pie

definitions.meaning: a shoemaker works at a last, the foot-shaped block shoes are made on
a fruit dish topped with scone-like dough is called by this name

explanation.surface: Someone who finally gets a pie to eat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at last' looks like 'finally', but a last is a shoemaker's block.
explanation.definitionFit: A shoe mender works at a last; a fruit pudding with a biscuit-dough crust shares the name.

clue.text: Co-ordinate a policy broadcast

indicators.note: broadcast means the words are spoken on air, so we go by sound

parts.note: a policy can be called a line, as in the party line

explanation.surface: Parties co-ordinate a single policy announcement on air.
explanation.walkthrough: 'broadcast' tells us A LINE is said aloud.
explanation.definitionFit: To align things is to bring them into agreement or arrangement, a sense of co-ordinate.

clue.text: Costs incurred by scuffle during trades

indicators.note: during means the scuffle happens inside the trades, so one word sits within the other

parts.note: trades are deals
a scuffle is a fray

explanation.surface: Fighting on the trading floor ran up costs.
explanation.definitionFit: Defraying is paying expenses, so these are payments of costs incurred.

clue.text: Creature from the deep lake

parts.note: the deep is a poetic name for the sea
L is the map abbreviation for lake

explanation.surface: An animal emerging from the waters of a deep lake.
explanation.definitionFit: A seal is a marine mammal, an example of a creature.

clue.text: Church elite must support one dairy product

indicators.note: in a down entry, the supporting part sits beneath, so these come below the numeral

parts.note: one is the Roman numeral I
CE is the Church of England
the elite is the cream, the best of a group

explanation.surface: The top clergy must back a single dairy item.
explanation.definitionFit: This frozen dessert is made from milk and cream, so it counts as a dairy product.

clue.text: Try, seeing enemies losing heart, perhaps

indicators.note: losing heart means the word enemies loses all its inside letters, keeping only its ends

parts.note: say, as in 'say ten', means perhaps or for example

explanation.surface: Attempt something, seeing your foes may be losing courage.
explanation.definitionFit: An essay is an attempt, an old sense still used formally.

clue.text: Promised disheartened pal, getting nicked

indicators.note: disheartened means the word pal has its middle letter taken out

parts.note: in cricket a batsman who nicks the ball has edged it

explanation.surface: A dejected friend, arrested, gave their word.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nicked' suggests arrested, but here it is the cricket sense.
explanation.definitionFit: Pledged means gave one's word, a direct synonym of promised.

clue.text: Rather inferior cider some brewed with no end of apples

indicators.note: brewed suggests a mixture, so the remaining letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: with no means the final letter of apples is dropped from the word some

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: end of means the last letter of the word apples

explanation.surface: Cider brewed without the last apples turns out second-rate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'end of apples' is S; 'with no' takes it from SOME, leaving OME; 'brewed' mixes CIDER and OME.
explanation.definitionFit: Mediocre means only middling in quality, which is a rather poor standard.

clue.text: Lawyer meeting patient, maybe a carrier

parts.note: a brief is informal for a barrister or lawyer
a doctor's patient is a case

explanation.surface: A lawyer meets a client who might be a disease carrier.
explanation.walkthrough: BRIEF is British slang for a lawyer.
explanation.definitionFit: A document holder with a handle is one example of a carrier.

clue.text: Material convinced on the radio

indicators.note: on the radio means the word is heard spoken, so we go by sound

parts.note: convinced means swayed

explanation.surface: Some broadcast stuff that persuaded listeners.
explanation.definitionFit: Suede is a soft napped leather, a kind of material.

clue.text: Perjurer ringing once oddly in a row

indicators.note: ringing means surrounding, so the word for perjurer goes round the other piece

parts.note: a perjurer lies under oath, a liar

indicators.note: oddly signals taking alternate letters of the word once

explanation.surface: A lying witness hemmed in, behaving strangely, standing in a queue.
explanation.definitionFit: Linear means arranged in a straight line, as things in a row are.

clue.text: Good! Fish, fish and fish

parts.note: a ray is a flat fish
a ling is a long fish of the cod family

explanation.surface: An angler delighted by a catch of fish after fish.
explanation.definitionFit: The grayling is a freshwater game fish of the salmon family.

clue.text: Newspaper article about length for such a coat

parts.note: rag is a disparaging word for a newspaper
an is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A newspaper feature on the length of a coat.
explanation.definitionFit: A raglan is a coat whose sleeves run up to the collar, named after Lord Raglan.

clue.text: Muzzle pug — not in buckles

indicators.note: buckles means bends out of shape, so the letters are reshuffled

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A pug's muzzle is not fastened with its buckles.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Muzzle' looks like a dog's, but it is the end of a gun barrel.
explanation.definitionFit: A gun's muzzle is its point, the business end of the weapon.

clue.text: Left dance drunk after graduate fair

indicators.note: after means the scrambled part follows the graduate

parts.note: BA is a Bachelor of Arts

indicators.note: drunk means reeling, so the letters are jumbled

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A tipsy dance after graduation, at the fair.
explanation.definitionFit: A fair or even-handed account is balanced, giving each side its due.

clue.text: Relative's friend is an easy target for criticism

parts.note: an aunt is a relative; the 's adds S
an ally is a friend

explanation.surface: A relative's friend is always being picked on.
explanation.walkthrough: An Aunt Sally is a British fairground game of throwing things at a dummy's head.
explanation.definitionFit: From that throwing game, the phrase came to mean anyone set up to be attacked or blamed.

clue.text: Attractive, feminine and making a deep impression

parts.note: etching cuts lines deep into a plate

explanation.surface: A lovely woman who leaves a lasting mark on people.
explanation.definitionFit: Fetching means charming or good-looking, a synonym of attractive.

clue.text: Element speaking languages before 10

indicators.note: before means the sound part comes ahead of the number
speaking means the word is said aloud, so we go by its sound

parts.note: tongues are languages
10 is ten

explanation.surface: Someone fluent in languages before ten o'clock is in their element.
explanation.definitionFit: Tungsten is a hard metallic chemical element, symbol W.

clue.text: Dump mainly serious adviser on course

parts.note: a tip is a rubbish dump

indicators.note: mainly means most of the word, so its final letter goes

parts.note: stern means serious

explanation.surface: A stern consultant on the golf course who dumps on you.
explanation.walkthrough: TIP is British for a rubbish dump.
explanation.definitionFit: At a racecourse, a tipster sells advice on which horses will win.

clue.text: Make up name to be assumed by popular doctor

parts.note: in means popular or fashionable

indicators.note: assumed means taken on board, so the name goes inside the doctor

parts.note: a vet is an animal doctor

explanation.surface: A well-liked doctor takes on a false name.
explanation.definitionFit: To invent a story is to make it up, fabricating it.

clue.text: Settler settling for support under table

indicators.note: settling suggests the letters shifting into a new position, a rearrangement

explanation.surface: A pioneer settling in needs something to hold up the table.
explanation.definitionFit: A trestle is a frame of legs on which a board rests, a support for a table.

clue.text: Extend agreement to cover results over target range, initially

indicators.note: to cover means the agreement wraps round the initials

parts.note: a pact is an agreement

indicators.note: initially means the first letters of results, over, target and range

explanation.surface: Lengthen a contract to include results above the target range.
explanation.definitionFit: To protract is to prolong or draw out in time, a synonym of extend.

clue.text: Gag miserable specimen with no wife

indicators.note: with no means the abbreviation for wife is taken out

parts.note: a wretch is a miserable creature

explanation.surface: Silence a sorry unmarried fellow.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gag' looks like silencing someone; here it means to heave.
explanation.definitionFit: To retch is to heave as if vomiting, which is the reflex sense of gag.

clue.text: Tipsy chef's hidden spirit

indicators.note: hidden means the letters lie concealed within the words tipsy chef's

explanation.surface: A drunken cook's secret spirit stash.
explanation.definitionFit: The psyche is the soul or mind, the inner spirit of a person.

clue.text: Belief system encountered in sacred orders

indicators.note: encountered in means found inside the words sacred orders

explanation.surface: A faith met with in holy religious orders.
explanation.definitionFit: A credo is a statement of beliefs, from the Latin for 'I believe'.

clue.text: Cook's stitch in time? No — the other way round!

definitions.note: cook's stands for 'cook is', a verb phrase; the definition is the verb cook

indicators.note: in normally puts the stitch word inside time
the other way round reverses the nesting, so time goes inside the stitch word

parts.note: to sew is to stitch

explanation.surface: A twist on the proverb 'a stitch in time saves nine'.
explanation.walkthrough: Stitch in time would put SEW inside T; 'the other way round' puts T inside SEW.
explanation.definitionFit: To stew is to cook slowly in liquid.

clue.text: Principle demonstrated by the empty grid

indicators.note: empty means the word the loses its middle, keeping its outer letters

parts.note: a net is a mesh or grid

explanation.surface: A rule illustrated by a blank grid.
explanation.definitionFit: A tenet is a doctrine or belief held as true, a principle.

clue.text: Lease revoked in disturbed client's mind

indicators.note: in places one piece inside the other
disturbed means the letters of client are thrown into disorder

parts.note: the possessive 's gives no letters

indicators.note: revoked is read as turned back, so the word is reversed

parts.note: to let is to lease

explanation.surface: A cancelled lease weighs on a troubled client's mind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lease' is the verb, as in to let a flat, so the word handed back is the one for leasing out, not the contract.
explanation.definitionFit: Intellect is the faculty of reasoning, essentially the mind.

clue.text: Rotten practice with company of French driver's rules

parts.note: high describes meat or game going off
a way of doing things is a practice
de is French for of

explanation.surface: Corrupt dealings by a French firm.
explanation.walkthrough: The Highway Code is the UK government's rulebook for road users.
explanation.definitionFit: This official booklet sets out the rules every British motorist must follow.
